stem: A lower-priced product is reasonably available and appears on the Massachusetts interchangeable-drug list, but the prescriber marked a valid no-substitution direction. Which facts control? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Determine whether the no-substitution direction is valid.
Confirm that the proposed product is listed as interchangeable.
Substitute any drug in the same therapeutic class.
Confirm that the proposed product is reasonably available at a lower retail price.
Honor a valid prescriber direction against substitution.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: Determine whether the no-substitution direction is valid. Confirm that the proposed product is listed as interchangeable. Confirm that the proposed product is reasonably available at a lower retail price. Honor a valid prescriber direction against substitution.

choice_analysis.A: Supported: Determine whether the no-substitution direction is valid.
choice_analysis.B: Supported: Confirm that the proposed product is listed as interchangeable.
choice_analysis.C: Not supported: Substitute any drug in the same therapeutic class.
choice_analysis.D: Supported: Confirm that the proposed product is reasonably available at a lower retail price.
choice_analysis.E: Supported: Honor a valid prescriber direction against substitution.

related_facts: A pharmacist dispenses a less expensive reasonably available interchangeable product listed under Massachusetts standards unless the prescriber validly indicates no substitution or another exception applies.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'Substitute any drug in the same therapeutic class.'
